_note: Evidence-qualified cached drug mapping for the ALS demonstration. Metformin is recorded in ChEMBL under the parent molecule identifier CHEMBL1431 and is approved for type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is included as an indirect AMPK-pathway modulator, not as a verified direct-binding ligand of PRKAA1. The relationship to ALS is a pathway-level drug-repurposing hypothesis and must not be presented as evidence that metformin treats ALS.

proteins_of_interest.role_in_disease: PRKAA1 encodes an AMPK catalytic subunit involved in cellular energy sensing. Abnormal AMPK signalling and energy-homeostasis disruption have been investigated in ALS motor-neuron models.

approved_drugs_targeting_protein.mechanism: Indirect activation of AMPK following changes in cellular energy status associated with inhibition of mitochondrial respiration; metformin is not represented as a direct PRKAA1-binding ligand.
approved_drugs_targeting_protein.known_safety_flags: contraindicated in severe renal impairment; risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis increases when drug clearance is substantially reduced
